title: The runner protocol and the design draft are published
why: EXP 021's frozen record cites two private inputs by sha256 only: the runner protocol (PROTOCOL-LAB02.md) and the design draft (DESIGN.md). A pre-registration should show how it will be run, not only what it predicts, so this amendment publishes both, screened. The record said the protocol's amendments and their resolutions are restated in FREEZE-NOTES-v1.1.md, which is true; but the protocol's own rules (the gates before any cell, the cell phases, the oracle, the plan's size and order, the runner decisions R1-R13) are restated nowhere. Nor are the design draft's own predictions, which the round-1 reviews answer, or its plan for the Labs page. Both are therefore published rather than left as hashes.
timing: Written after the pre-registration was published (odin-rnd #83, merged 2026-10-25 20:11:56Z). It adds documents only. Whether any counted cell started before this amendment merged is recorded by the runner, whose counted cells carry the publish sha; this amendment changes no rule they ran under.

substitutionRule: Machine names (the Windows PC, the PC, the Mac), two paths in the private repository and the private mission-ledger path were replaced with neutral wording, the same rule as the record's publicCopy. Each `was` masks the private string. The lab checked privately that undoing each file's substitutions with the unmasked strings gives back its sourceSha256; the inverse mapping is withheld, so that check is the lab's attestation. File names inside the experiment's own runner are kept. 'Lab 02' is kept as written; the record's naming block maps it to Lab 03 (failover).

The record's source.inputs entries for the two documents ('published: no') describe the record as frozen; this amendment is where they are published.
